r.title: Category rules
r.desc: If a new transaction's name contains the text, it gets that category.
r.none: No rules yet. Add one above, or let an AI make them in Set up with an AI.
r.dup: There is already a rule for that text
r.added: Rule added. {n} uncategorized transaction now in {c}. | Rule added. {n} uncategorized transactions now in {c}.
r.addedNew: Rule added. It applies to new transactions.
r.newGo: New transactions with "{k}" now go to {c}.
r.move: Move {n} past transaction too | Move {n} past transactions too
r.foot: The first rule that matches wins. A category you set by hand is never changed.

tr.title: Tag rules
tr.desc: If a new transaction's name contains the text, it gets these tags.
tr.none: No tag rules yet. Add one above. Example: “netflix” adds the tag “streaming”.
tr.last: A tag rule needs at least one tag. Delete the rule instead.
tr.addedNew: Rule added. New transactions that contain “{k}” get {tags}.
tr.updatedNone: Rule updated. No other transactions need the tag.
tr.from: From now on, new transactions that contain “{k}” get
tr.have: transaction you already have matches. | transactions you already have match.
tr.foot: Tags come on top of the category, and one rule can add several. When you add a rule, you can also tag the transactions you already have.

n.title: Display names
n.desc: Show a clearer name for an entry. The bank's own text stays as it is.
n.name: Name
n.none: No name rules yet. Example: if Memo contains “Acme Ltd” → Salary.
n.needBoth: Type the text to match and the name
n.needBothEdit: A name rule needs text to match and a name
n.foot: Your rules and reports still use the bank's text. The first rule that matches wins, and a name you give one entry by hand always wins. To name one entry, open it and use Display name.

gen.cardDesc: If a payment from your bank contains the text, it is the bill of a credit card. It is not counted as spending, because each purchase is already counted on the card.
gen.cardNone: No rules of your own yet. Mark one card payment in Activity and the app offers to make one for you, or add one above.
gen.cardPh: Text from the bank line, for example ישראכרט חיוב
gen.cardAuto: Recognised automatically, with no rule: {list}. Also any bank payment equal to what a card was charged on that day.
gen.cardShort: Type some text from the bank line, for example “ישראכרט חיוב”.

ai.title: Let an AI make your categories
ai.desc: Categories, rules, tags, display names, card payments and salary, made for your own spending, with any AI chat you already use.
ai.privacy: The app puts each payment into a category (like Food or Car) so you can see where your money goes. Setting this up by hand, shop by shop, takes a long time. Here an AI chat does it for you: it reads the names of the shops and payers in your transactions and writes rules, so new payments are sorted on their own. Follow the 3 steps below. You check every suggestion before anything is added. Only the names leave the app, never amounts, dates or accounts.
ai.s1: A file with the one name in your transactions. | A file with the {n} different names in your transactions.
ai.s2: Copy the instructions, paste them into an AI chat (for example ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini), and attach the file.
ai.s3: The AI first shows you a table to check. When you are happy with it, it gives a file or a block of text. Upload it here to see what it would add.
ai.pasteQ: The AI gave text, not a file?
ai.bad: This does not look like an answer made with these instructions. Ask the AI again, or paste its whole answer.
ai.none: Nothing new to add: everything in it is already here.
ai.prev: This will add. Uncheck what you don't want:
ai.sorts: It also sorts {n} entry that has no category yet. Entries you sorted yourself stay as they are. | It also sorts {n} entries that have no category yet. Entries you sorted yourself stay as they are.
ai.skipped: {n} line was left out (a category that is not in the file, or a text that is too short or too long). | {n} lines were left out (a category that is not in the file, or a text that is too short or too long).
ai.done: Added {n} item. Undo is in the message and in the change history. | Added {n} items. Undo is in the message and in the change history.
ai.prompt:
I use a money app and want my spending sorted into categories. The attached file lists the names that appear in my transactions (shops and payers), how many times each appears, and whether money went out or came in. It also lists what I already have: categories, tags, display names, card payment texts and salary texts. Don't repeat those.

Please work out:
1. categories: 8 to 25 clear categories that fit these transactions. Reuse my existing categories where they fit. Mark categories for money coming in with "income": true. Write the names in English, short and simple.
2. rules: for each name you can sort, a short piece of it (at least 2 letters) that always appears in it and does not appear in unrelated names, and the category it belongs to. One rule can cover many names, for example a chain with many branches. Every category used in a rule must be in your categories list or in mine.
3. tagRules: only if clearly useful, a short piece of a name and one or more tags (a short word, for example a trip or a project).
4. displayNames: only where the bank's text is messy (codes, numbers, cut-off words), a short piece of it and a clean, short name to show instead.
5. cardPayments: texts of bank lines that pay the bill of a credit card company.
6. salary: texts of money coming in that is really salary from an employer. Not other income.

Leave out names you are not sure about. I will sort those myself.

First, before any file, show me here in the chat a preview table with one row per name: Name, Category, Tags, Display name (empty when the name stays the same). Below it, short lists of the card payment texts and the salary texts you found. Then ask me to confirm or correct it.

Only after I confirm, give the result as a downloadable .json file if you can make files, otherwise as one JSON code block. Use exactly this shape:
ai.nCards: {n} card payment text | {n} card payment texts
ai.dCards: A bank line with one of these texts pays a credit card bill. It is not counted as spending, because each purchase is already counted on the card.
ai.dSalary: Income with one of these texts is marked as Salary.

mi.title: Money coming in
mi.desc: If money coming in holds the text (in its transaction name or the payer), it is a Salary or Money back, as you pick here.
mi.none: No rules of your own yet. Add a payer above, for example your employer.
mi.ph: Payer or text, for example wix
mi.short: Type text from the payer or the transaction name, for example “wix”.
mi.added: Rule added. It matches 1 entry of money coming in you already have. | Rule added. It matches {n} entries of money coming in you already have.
mi.addedNew: Rule added. Money coming in like this follows it from now on.
mi.auto: With no rule: money that came in on a credit card is Money back, and all other money coming in is Income. Nothing is decided from words in the text.
